title: Most people read Book of Joshua chapter 24 like it’s a farewell speech.
paragraphs: Most people read Book of Joshua chapter 24 like it’s a farewell speech.
And if you miss that, you miss everything.
Joshua is old. The battles are over. The land has been divided. From the outside, it looks like a peaceful ending… a leader giving final advice.
“The LORD, the God of Israel, says: ‘Long ago your fathers lived beyond the Euphrates… and they served other gods.’” (Joshua 24:2)
Because here’s what most people don’t realize… Joshua isn’t trying to inspire them.
He walks them through everything God did—calling Abraham, delivering from Egypt, parting the Red Sea, defeating enemies, giving them land they didn’t earn.
“I gave you a land on which you had not labored and cities that you had not built.” (Joshua 24:13)
“Now therefore fear the LORD and serve him in sincerity and in faithfulness. Put away the gods…” (Joshua 24:14)
That means they still had them.
After all God had done… they were still holding onto idols.
You’ve seen God move. You’ve been rescued, forgiven, spared, carried—and still there are things you won’t let go of.
And then comes the line everyone quotes—but almost no one fully understands:
“Choose this day whom you will serve…” (Joshua 24:15)
People treat that like a motivational slogan.
There is no neutral ground in this courtroom.
Your comfort. Your sin. Your image. Your control.
But here’s the detail most people miss—the moment everything turns.
“We also will serve the LORD, for he is our God.” (Joshua 24:18)
“You are not able to serve the LORD, for he is a holy God. He is a jealous God; he will not forgive your transgressions or your sins.” (Joshua 24:19)
Because he sees what they don’t.
Their words are louder than their repentance.
They think this is about willpower.
God is not looking for enthusiasm.
And that’s the fracture line most people step over without noticing.
You can say the right things and still be spiritually dead.
You can declare loyalty and still be enslaved to sin.
You can choose God with your mouth and reject Him with your life.
“Then put away the foreign gods that are among you, and incline your heart to the LORD…” (Joshua 24:23)
Because the law exposes what you cannot fix.
It reveals that you are not able.
Because the story doesn’t end in Joshua.
Where Joshua says, “You are not able,” the Gospel declares:
“But God shows his love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” (Romans 5:8)
Where the law demands perfection, grace provides a Savior.
“By grace you have been saved through faith… not a result of works.” (Ephesians 2:8–9)
Jesus doesn’t just call you to choose.
He makes a way for you to be changed.
He takes the punishment Joshua warned about.
He satisfies the holiness you could never meet.
And then He gives you a new heart.
Joshua’s speech isn’t just a call to choose God.
It’s a revelation that you can’t truly serve Him without being transformed by Him.
So now you’re standing in that same courtroom.
And the question isn’t whether you’ll say the right words.
It’s whether you’ll finally surrender the things you’ve been hiding behind.
Say it plainly—“I’ve been holding onto idols.”
And if you’re ready to go deeper—to be corrected, challenged, and built in real faith, not empty words—step into what most people avoid but desperately need:
Because there are only two directions from here.
Keep saying “I will serve God”… while holding onto everything that separates you from Him.
Or finally surrender—and let Jesus do what you never could.
